title: Quantitative Reasoning for Decision Makers
summary: A practical introduction to reading data, probability and statistical evidence for managers who rely on analysis but do not produce it.
participants: Business and operations staff who review reports
objectives: Interpret common summary measures and recognise when they mislead
Reason about probability, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem in everyday decisions
Understand what a confidence interval and a hypothesis test do and do not show
Ask better questions about the assumptions behind an analysis
topics: Types of data and choosing appropriate charts
Mean, median, mode and measures of dispersion
Correlation versus causation
Probability, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem
Binomial, Poisson and normal distributions
Sampling distributions and standard error
Hypothesis testing, errors and significance levels

example_agenda.detail: Variable types, charts and summary measures, with examples of misleading averages.
Conditional probability and Bayes' theorem applied to business scenarios.
Sampling, confidence intervals and what a test result really means.
A checklist exercise reviewing a sample report.

customisation: Examples drawn from the organisation's own sector
Use of the organisation's anonymised reports as case material
Pre-workshop survey to gauge participants' comfort with numbers

title: Excel Analytics for Teams
summary: Hands-on training in the Excel functions, lookups, PivotTables and charts that teams use to analyse and report data every day.
participants: Analysts who work mainly in spreadsheets
objectives: Import, clean and structure data in Excel
Use lookup, logical and statistical functions correctly
Build and format PivotTables and PivotCharts
Consolidate results from multiple worksheets into a clear summary
topics: Basic, text, date and time functions
Importing data, text to columns and removing duplicates
Absolute and relative cell referencing
LOOKUP functions
IF, nested IF and AND/OR/NOT
SUMIF, COUNTIF and statistical functions
PivotTables and PivotCharts
Chart techniques and worksheet formatting

example_agenda.detail: Importing, cleaning, grouping and referencing.
Lookup, logical and conditional statistical functions.
Summarising and slicing data interactively.
Consolidation, chart techniques and formatting a finished report.

customisation: Exercises built on the organisation's own anonymised data
Focus on the reports the team produces regularly
Pre-workshop skills survey to set the starting level

title: Python & R for Data Analysis
summary: An introduction to programming for analysis in R and Python, from reading data to producing summary statistics and plots.
participants: Researchers and engineers new to programming
Technical staff who need reproducible analysis
objectives: Write and run simple scripts in R and Python
Read data from files, manipulate it and handle common errors
Produce descriptive statistics and frequency distributions
Create clear plots of data
topics: How R works: objects, data in files, sequences and matrix computation
Python basics: values, types, variables, expressions
Conditionals and loops
Debugging syntax, runtime and semantic errors
Descriptive statistics and frequency distributions
Discrete and continuous probability distributions in R
Graphics and plots

example_agenda.detail: Objects, reading and writing data, and simple calculations.
Variables, control flow and reading a text file.
Summary statistics and frequency tables in both languages.
Producing and saving charts, and a short end-to-end exercise.

customisation: Choice of R only, Python only, or both
Exercises using the organisation's own anonymised datasets
Pre-workshop skills survey and environment set-up check

title: Applied Machine Learning
summary: A practical tour of core machine learning methods, how they are trained and how to evaluate them honestly.
participants: Analysts and developers with some programming experience
Data teams starting machine learning projects
objectives: Distinguish supervised and unsupervised learning and choose suitable techniques
Explain gradient descent and the bias-variance trade-off
Train and compare classical classifiers on real data
Evaluate models with accuracy, precision and recall
topics: Types of learning and steps in a machine learning project
Constrained and unconstrained optimisation; gradient descent
Linear regression, goodness of fit and bias-variance trade-off
Decision trees, bagging and random forests
Support-vector machines and naive Bayes
k-means and k-nearest neighbours
Gradient boosting
Model evaluation measures

example_agenda.detail: Learning types, data representation and the machine learning workflow.
Gradient descent, least squares and the bias-variance trade-off.
Trees, random forests, SVM, naive Bayes and kNN in practice.
Accuracy, precision, recall and comparing models fairly.
Participants build and present a small model end to end.

customisation: Use cases from the organisation's sector
Project work on the organisation's own anonymised data
Choice of Python or R for exercises
Pre-workshop skills survey

title: Statistical Modelling Workshop
summary: Building, checking and interpreting regression models, including regularised and logistic regression.
participants: Analysts who already use basic statistics
Marketing and operations teams using predictive models
objectives: Fit and interpret simple and multiple regression models
Use cross-validation to compare models
Apply ridge and lasso regularisation to control overfitting
Model binary outcomes with logistic regression and discriminant analysis
topics: Scatter diagrams, correlation and least squares
Coefficient of determination
Multiple and polynomial regression
Cross-validation
Ridge (Tikhonov) and lasso regression
Logistic regression for binary outcomes
Discriminant analysis

example_agenda.detail: Least squares, interpretation and fit.
Multiple and polynomial regression with cross-validation.
Ridge and lasso in practice.
Logistic regression and discriminant analysis with a worked case.

customisation: Case studies matched to the organisation's sector
Exercises using the organisation's own anonymised data
Choice of R, Python or SPSS for demonstrations

title: Data Visualization Workshop
summary: Principles and practice of clear, honest charts for reports, dashboards and presentations.
participants: Anyone who produces charts for reports or presentations
objectives: Match data types to suitable visual encodings and chart types
Use colour deliberately to distinguish, represent and highlight
Show distributions, proportions and trends effectively
Critique and improve existing charts
topics: Mapping data onto aesthetics; scales and axes
Colour scales
Visualising amounts: bars, dot plots and heatmaps
Distributions: histograms, ECDFs and Q-Q plots
Proportions: pie, side-by-side and stacked bars
Trends, smoothing and time-series decomposition
Geospatial data: choropleths and cartograms

example_agenda.detail: Aesthetics, scales and coordinate systems.
Colour choices and charts for comparing quantities.
Choosing the right chart for each question.
Participants redesign charts from their own work.

customisation: Chart clinic using the organisation's own reports
Exercises in Excel, R or Python depending on tools in use
Alignment with the organisation's style guidelines

title: Research & Analytical Methods
summary: Research design, sampling, experimental design and clear technical write-ups for teams that run studies.
participants: Policy and programme staff who commission studies
objectives: Frame a research problem and choose a suitable research design
Select and justify a sampling design for a survey
Plan a basic designed experiment and its analysis
Prepare well-structured technical documents and presentations in LaTeX and Beamer
topics: Research process, problem definition and literature review
Models, model classification and simulation studies
Sample surveys, sampling frames and steps in a survey
Simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic sampling
CRD, RBD, LSD and factorial experiments
LaTeX documents, tables, figures and mathematics
BibTeX bibliographies and Beamer presentations

example_agenda.detail: From research question to research design and literature review.
Choosing and comparing sampling designs.
Principles of experimental design and ANOVA-based analysis.
LaTeX, BibTeX and Beamer for reports and presentations.

customisation: Examples from the organisation's field of research
Review of a current or planned study as a case
Optional extended LaTeX lab

title: Quality Control for Operations
summary: Control charts and acceptance sampling for teams responsible for product and service quality.
objectives: Distinguish chance from assignable causes of variation
Construct and interpret variables and attributes control charts
Choose subgroup size and sampling frequency sensibly
Understand single and double acceptance sampling plans
topics: Quality, productivity and quality costs
Statistical basis of control charts and control limits
Rational subgroups, patterns, warning limits and ARL
X-bar and R charts; X-bar and s charts
p and np charts
Single and double sampling plans, OC and ASN functions

example_agenda.detail: Quality concepts and chance versus assignable causes.
Building X-bar, R and s charts.
p and np charts and reading patterns.
Designing and comparing sampling plans.

customisation: Exercises using the organisation's own anonymised process data
Examples specific to manufacturing or service settings
Templates for charts in the tools the team already uses

Recognise where NoSQL stores such as MongoDB and Cassandra fit

Hadoop architecture, HDFS and cluster modes
MapReduce phases, combiners and joins
Pig Latin and Hive
Spark applications, RDDs and Spark SQL
Building a data pipeline with PySpark and Hive
NoSQL with MongoDB and Cassandra

Architecture, file operations and MapReduce word count.
Querying and transforming data at scale.
Spark applications and a PySpark pipeline.

Sector-specific examples such as retail or marketing data
